To find out how long it will take Bob to dig the hole, we need to determine the total volume of earth he needs to remove and then multiply that by the time it takes to shovel one cubic foot.

**Step 1: Calculate the volume of the hole.**
The hole is a rectangular prism with the following dimensions:
*   Length ($L$) = 6 feet
*   Width ($W$) = 4 feet
*   Depth ($D$) = 3 feet

The formula for the volume ($V$) of a rectangular prism is:
$$V = L \times W \times D$$

Substituting the given values:
$$V = 6 \text{ ft} \times 4 \text{ ft} \times 3 \text{ ft}$$
$$V = 24 \text{ ft}^2 \times 3 \text{ ft}$$
$$V = 72 \text{ cubic feet}$$

So, Bob needs to shovel 72 cubic feet of earth.

**Step 2: Calculate the total time required.**
We are told that it takes Bob 3 seconds to shovel 1 cubic foot of earth. To find the total time, we multiply the total volume by the time per cubic foot.

$$\text{Total Time} = \text{Volume} \times \text{Time per cubic foot}$$
$$\text{Total Time} = 72 \text{ cubic feet} \times 3 \text{ seconds/cubic foot}$$
$$\text{Total Time} = 216 \text{ seconds}$$

**Conclusion:**
It will take Bob 216 seconds to dig the hole.

Final answer: 216
